text:
STL trailed 2-0 after one period and still won going away, which fits a game that tilted hard once the second period started. CBJ out-chanced STL in the first, 0.95 expected goals to 0.55, and took the lead on a Valeri Nichushkin deflection and a Kent Johnson wrist shot with 12 seconds left in the period. That second goal came on a 6% chance, a gift from a period STL mostly played well.

The middle frame belonged to the home side. STL generated 1.48 expected goals to CBJ's 0.29 and scored three times in about six and a half minutes: Jake Neighbours on a slap shot, then Jimmy Snuggerud twice. His second came on a 2% chance, the least likely goal of the night, but it arrived because Dylan Holloway kept setting him up. Holloway assisted on both of Snuggerud's goals and on Neighbours' tally, three helps in all, with his line owning a 1.08 to 0.60 edge in on-ice expected goals.

Cole Sillinger tied it at 3-3 early in the third, and Jonatan Berggren answered 2:42 later with a 30% look. Pavel Buchnevich added an empty-looking insurance goal at 19:17 on a 54% chance. By the full-game numbers, STL's 3.67 expected goals to CBJ's 1.77 gave them a 74% chance to win in a replay of every shot. Jordan Binnington gave back 1.23 goals against expectation, but the skaters outran him. Jet Greaves was 0.86 goals below expectation behind a team that blocked 19 shots.
